gap: The r2 ink split is fixed (single #0d1b5e at 14.4:1, matching Wave's #001b66 at 14.5:1), so the loss is now purely the type scale: our headline leading is set at roughly 1.02, leaving only 5 device px (2.5 CSS) of clearance between the descenders of 'that speaks' and the ascenders of 'your language', and only 47 device px (23 CSS) between the headline block and the body, where Wave leaves 45 and 98 device px (22 and 49 CSS) on a headline of the same cap height. Open headline line-height to about 1.12 and the headline-to-body gap to 44-48 CSS, and soften the display face: the current high-contrast didone reads editorial-fashion, while Wave's moderate-contrast transitional serif is what makes it read as a calm financial institution.
